messages:
sam: Heads-up — after the routing-priority rollout I'm seeing slow initial chart renders in the console canary (EU). Heatmap + sparklines have a ~150-200ms extra main-thread hit on first paint. Anyone else seeing this?

maya: saw it too. Looks correlated with the prefetch policy change + kv-cache TTL bump earlier today. Cache-miss rate for chart tile requests jumped from ~12% to ~48% during the canary window.

eli: confirmed on my end, reproduces on dev and canary with user agent emulation. Likely a prefetch ordering issue — telemetry payloads are being prioritized over bundle + chart tile prefetch.

sam: exact config that changed is the new routing/prefetch policy push. snippet from the rollout: 
```
console.prefetch.priority = [
  "telemetry",
  "core-ui",
  "charts"
]
console.prefetch.concurrency = 3
kv_cache.ttl_ms = 60000
```

jia: that ordering will starve chart assets on cold loads. two quick mitigation options: bump charts up in priority for canary OR temporarily increase prefetch.concurrency for canary.

maya: +1 for priority bump for canary only. Also the new client build inlines the heavy svg helper lib which made first-paint worse when chart code executes on main thread. splitting to offscreen/worker helps.

eli: agree. short-term: canary flag to set charts -> core-ui priority. medium-term: move svg parsing to offscreen canvas worker and split that chunk.

sam: propose: 1) roll a targeted canary rollback of the routing-priority change in EU, 2) patch the canary flag to set charts to higher priority, 3) run a perf iteration that increases prefetch.concurrency to 6 and measures kvcache miss behavior.

oncall-bot: deploy scheduled — rolling canary patch to EU at 2026-03-21T14:30:00Z (runbook RB-112).

devx-bot: created INF-789: "console-chart-prefetch-route-fallback" and assigned to @jia and @maya.

jia: I'll add a synthetic test that toggles prefetch.priority and measures first-paint + cache miss. quick check command to pull the telemetry traces: 
```bash
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $INFR_TOKEN\" \"https://telemetry.redwood.dev/api/v1/trace?service=console&env=canary&period=5m\" | jq '.spans | map(select(.name|test("chart|prefetch")))'
```

maya: noted. also filing a tiny client hotfix to split the svg helper out of the main chart bundle (will open PR later today).

eli: after rollback + canary flag we should watch for churn in routing metrics (route fanout, queue latency). If stable after 30m we can promote the fix to broader canary.

sam: plan sounds good. I'll coordinate the rollback window and notify support/CS. thanks all. :thumbsup:
